questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'hit the jackpot'?

options.text: To win a game of cards by cheating
To achieve sudden, tremendous success or fortune
To suffer a heavy loss in business
To damage public property

questions.explanation: 'Hit the jackpot' ka arth achanak behad badi kamyabi, fayda ya dhan prapt karna hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question: The idiom 'leave no stone unturned' means:

options.text: To engage in manual construction work
To search thoroughly and do everything possible to achieve an aim
To cause physical obstruction on public pathways
To ignore small details in an investigation

questions.explanation: 'Leave no stone unturned' ka matlab hota hai har sambhav rasta apnana aur koi kasar na chhodna.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question: What does 'read between the lines' mean?

options.text: To identify typographical errors in printed texts
To understand the implicit, unstated meaning beyond literal words
To read a document with extreme speed
To underline key words in a statute

questions.explanation: 'Read between the lines' ka matlab hota hai chhipe huye ya ankahe arth ko samajhna.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Sentence Context Isolation Protocol.

questions.question: The phrase 'won't break the bank' implies that an item:

options.text: Is strictly illegal under banking laws
Is reasonably priced and affordable
Will cause financial bankruptcy
Is available only through bank loans

questions.explanation: 'Won't break the bank' ka matlab hota hai ki koi vastu budget ke andar hai aur affordable hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-11: Financial & Resource Context Precision.

questions.question:
In the sentence:
"Accepting the punitive demotion was a bitter pill for the senior officer to swallow."
The underlined expression means:

options.text: Consuming an unpalatable medication
An unpleasant fact or circumstance that must be endured
An unfair medical leave granted by authorities
Refusing to comply with disciplinary sanctions

questions.explanation: 'A bitter pill to swallow' ka arth aisi apriy sacchayi ya punishment hoti hai jise majbooran bardasht karna pade.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question:
Select the closest meaning of 'the last straw' in this sentence:
"The clerk tolerated long working hours, but the denial of festival leave was the last straw."

options.text: A physical piece of dry grass found in office records
The final problem in a series of troubles that makes the situation intolerable
The primary initial complaint lodged by the union
A trivial matter easily resolved by conversation

questions.explanation: 'The last straw' musibaton ki series ka aakhri aisa event hota hai jiske baad vyakti ka sabra toot jata hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Sentence Context Isolation Protocol.

questions.question:
"The administrative committee and the bar association do not see eye to eye on court timings."
This means the two parties:

options.text: Refuse to look at each other during hearings
Are in complete disagreement on the issue
Have agreed to reconcile their past disputes
Have identical optical requirements

questions.explanation: 'See eye to eye' ka matlab agree hona hota hai; 'do not see eye to eye' ka matlab asahmat hona (disagreement) hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-13: Reconciliation vs Simple Agreement.

questions.question: What does 'hear through the grapevine' mean in official workplace communication?

options.text: To receive communication via registered postal dispatch
To hear news through informal rumors and unofficial gossip
To inspect agricultural estates under high court receiver ship
To access secured digital court databases

questions.explanation: 'Hear through the grapevine' ka matlab anaupcharik afwahon ya gossip ke zariye khabar sunna hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-12: Disclosure vs Rumour Disambiguation.

questions.question: "In a joint project, every officer must pull his weight." This means each officer should:

options.text: Exercise in the gymnasium regularly
Do his fair share of the collective work
Assume absolute unilateral control of decisions
Carry heavy case bundles physically

questions.explanation: 'Pull one's weight' ka matlab group ya team mein apne hisse ka poora kaam imaandari se karna hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question:
Complete the sentence with the appropriate idiom:
"When the appellate bench set aside the preliminary decree, the litigants were ________."

options.text: on cloud nine
back to square one
ahead of their time
worth their weight in gold

questions.explanation: Decree set aside hone par case dobara shuruat ke point par chala gaya, isliye 'back to square one' aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Idiom Sentence Completion Strategy.

questions.question: "The petitioner filed an amended affidavit at the eleventh hour." This means the affidavit was filed:

options.text: Precisely at eleven o'clock in the morning
At the latest possible moment before the deadline
Well in advance of the scheduled hearing
During the post-lunch judicial session

questions.explanation: 'At the eleventh hour' ka arth aakhri moment ya sabse late possible samay par hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Time & Frequency Boundary Precision.

questions.question: Which idiom describes a family that spends all their meager earnings on daily survival without savings?

options.text: Live from hand to mouth
Burn the midnight oil
Play it by ear
Bite the bullet

questions.explanation: 'Live from hand to mouth' ka matlab roz ki aamdani par guzara karna hota hai bina kisi bachat ke.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-11: Financial & Resource Context Precision.

questions.question: If an officer is 'down in the dumps', he is feeling:

options.text: Extremely triumphant and proud
Dejected, depressed, and unhappy
Physically energetic and active
Curious about judicial precedents

questions.explanation: 'Down in the dumps' ka matlab udaas, dukhi ya niraash hona hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Emotion & Psychological Tone Alignment.

questions.question: What does 'bury the hatchet' mean?

options.text: To conceal illegal weapons under earth
To end a feud and establish peace
To initiate criminal proceedings
To dismiss staff members summarily

questions.explanation: 'Bury the hatchet' purani dushmani ya jhagda bhula kar aapsi sulah kar lene ko kehte hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-13: Reconciliation vs Simple Agreement.

questions.question: "The committee members cannot sit on the fence during this crucial vote." This means they must not:

options.text: Climb physical boundary railings
Remain neutral or delay making a firm decision
Cast multiple conflicting ballots
Walk out of the assembly hall

questions.explanation: 'Sit on the fence' ka arth neutral rehna ya faisla lene mein der karna hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question:
Distinguish between 'cold feet' and 'cold shoulder':
Which sentence uses 'cold shoulder' correctly?

options.text: The applicant got a cold shoulder and ran away in fear before entering the viva room.
After siding with the rival candidate, Mohan was given the cold shoulder by his old colleagues.
He put on a warm coat because his cold shoulder was shivering in winter.
The whistleblower developed a cold shoulder and refused to sign the affidavit.

questions.explanation: 'Cold shoulder' kisi ko deliberate ignore ya upeksha karne ke liye lagta hai (Sentence B). 'Cold feet' dar se pichhe hatne ke liye lagta hai (jo sentences A aur D mein misuse kiya gaya hai).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Distinguishing Confusing Lookalike Idioms.

questions.question: When workers decide to 'call it a day', they intend to:

options.text: Permanently resign from their government positions
Stop working for the remainder of the current day
Declare an indefinite general strike
Work throughout the midnight hours

questions.explanation: 'Call it a day' ka matlab aaj ke liye kaam band karna hota hai. Permanently chhodne ke liye 'call it quits' lagta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Time & Frequency Boundary Precision.

questions.question: "The construction firm was penalized for cutting corners during the court annex renovation." Here 'cutting corners' means:

options.text: Rounding off the sharp angles of stone blocks
Taking improper shortcuts by compromising on quality and standards
Finishing the contract several weeks ahead of schedule
Terminating the workers' contracts prematurely

questions.explanation: 'Cut corners' ka arth paisa ya samay bachane ke liye galat tareeqe ya substandard shortcuts lena hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question: Both 'spill the beans' and 'let the cat out of the bag' denote revealing secrets. However, 'let the cat out of the bag' most frequently describes:

options.text: Releasing captured laboratory animals
Inadvertently disclosing a surprise or secret plan
Giving false testimony before a magistrate
Blackmailing public servants

questions.explanation: 'Let the cat out of the bag' aksar kisi chhipayi hui surprise planning ya secret ko galti se zaahir kar dene ke liye use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-12: Disclosure vs Rumour Disambiguation.

questions.question:
Spot the error in the underlined portion of the sentence:
"To put the matter (A) / in the nutshell, (B) / the appeal lacks merit (C) / and stands dismissed. (D)"

options.text: Part A
Part B
Part C
Part D

questions.explanation: Rule RC-04 ke anusaar, established idiom 'in a nutshell' hota hai, na ki '*in the nutshell*'. Part B mein article distortion error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Fixed Phraseology & Non-Substitution Law.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses the idiom correctly without structural distortion?

options.text: The directors do not see eyes to eyes on the fiscal deficit.
The directors do not see eye to eye on the fiscal deficit.
The directors do not see an eye to an eye on the fiscal deficit.
The directors do not look eye to eye on the fiscal deficit.

questions.explanation: Correct fixed phrase 'see eye to eye' hai. Options A aur C mein nouns ko pluralize ya article add kiya gaya hai jo incorrect hai. Option D mein verb badal di gayi hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Fixed Phraseology & Non-Substitution Law.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence conforming to subject-possessive concord:

options.text: The young women maintained one's cool during the fire alarm.
The young women maintained her cool during the fire alarm.
The young women maintained their cool during the fire alarm.
The young women maintained theirs cool during the fire alarm.

questions.explanation: Rule RC-05 ke mutabiq, plural subject 'The young women' ke sath plural possessive adjective 'their' aayega ('maintained their cool').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Subject-Possessive Concord Rule in Idioms.

questions.question: The registrar instructed the staff to execute the tender process 'by the book'. This means:

options.text: By reading books aloud during meetings
In strict accordance with established official rules and laws
Without maintaining any written accounts
According to personal discretionary opinions

questions.explanation: 'By the book' ka arth sabhi established rules, laws aur procedure ka aksharasah strict palan karna hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question:
Select the meaning of 'in black and white':
"The high court registry required all undertakings to be submitted in black and white."

options.text: Printed only in monochrome ink
In official written or printed form
Without containing any legal arguments
Supported by photographic evidence

questions.explanation: 'In black and white' ka established legal aur administrative meaning 'in written or printed form' (likhit roop mein) hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question:
"The bench declared the illegal appointment orders null and void."
Here 'null and void' means:

options.text: Legally binding and enforceable
Having no legal force or validity
Kept in temporary abeyance
Circulated to all subordinate courts

questions.explanation: 'Null and void' legal aur administrative English ka established phrase hai jiska arth 'having no legal validity' (shunya aur nishprabhavi) hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question: Why is implementing complete automation described as a 'double-edged sword'?

options.text: Because it cuts down physical paper files
Because it brings significant benefits but also entails serious potential risks
Because it costs twice as much as manual processing
Because it is strictly forbidden under judicial service rules

questions.explanation: 'A double-edged sword' aisi niti ya tool hota hai jiske acche laabh ke sath-sath barabar khatre (benefits and hazards) dono hote hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question: The idiom 'face the music' refers to:

options.text: Attending a classical cultural program
Confronting and accepting the unpleasant consequences of one's actions
Appreciating harmonious legal arguments
Listening to radio news broadcasts

questions.explanation: 'Face the music' ka arth apni galti ya apradh ke dushparinam aur daant ko jhelna hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question: "By obsessing over petty font margins, the editor could not see the forest for the trees." This implies:

options.text: The editor was fond of forestry and botany
He was so focused on trivial details that he failed to perceive the overall situation
He cleared the document room of paper clutter
He was visually impaired

questions.explanation: 'Not see the forest for the trees' ka matlab chhoti details mein itna ulajh jana hota hai ki main picture ya broad reality nazar na aaye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question: The idiom 'call a spade a spade' emphasizes:

options.text: Using accurate agricultural tools
Speaking the blunt, direct truth without euphemisms or evasion
Playing card games competitively
Accusing innocent persons falsely

questions.explanation: 'Call a spade a spade' ka matlab sach ko bina kisi laag-lapet ke bilkul spasht aur seedhe shabdon mein bolna hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.

questions.question: "With multiple vigilance inquiries ordered against the agency, the writing was on the wall." This indicates:

options.text: Graffiti was painted on the office walls
There were clear, unmistakable signs of impending downfall or failure
The agency received formal commendations
The inquiry officers painted notice boards

questions.explanation: 'The writing is on the wall' ka arth aane wale vinash, downfall ya asafalta ke spasht sanket hona hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Literal vs Figurative Meaning Filter.
